thread.title: Weekend roundup: Be careful with marijuana stocks | 10 years of bitcoin | Stock dividend cuts

author: Philip van Doorn
title: Weekend roundup: Be careful with marijuana stocks | 10 years of bitcoin | Stock dividend cuts
text:
MarketWatch rounds up 10 of its most interesting topics over the past week.
1. Take a hard look when picking marijuana stocks A company that says it produces marijuana-based products may do nothing of the sort .
Related: The push for legalizing marijuana in the U.S. will soon run out of steam
2. Happy anniversary, bitcoin! The pioneering cryptocurrency has been around for 10 years. Here’s a sampling of BTCUSD, -0.77% coverage:
• The round numbers that show just how far bitcoin has come in 10 years
• Bitcoin trades higher on 10th birthday, still down 67% from all-time high
• How bitcoin has failed to achieve Satoshi Nakamoto’s original intent
• Bitcoin’s average trading range has narrowed nearly 90%, says analyst
• Barron’s: Bitcoin is 10 years old — here are 5 questions for the next decade
3. Brutal dividend cuts and warnings that more are possible General Electric GE, -3.03% cut its quarterly dividend to a penny a share this week, which wasn’t a surprise, while Anheuser-Busch InBev SA BUD, -0.22% reduced its interim dividend by half on Oct. 25. Here are five more companies that may be forced to reduce their dividend payouts .
4. A disturbing map Whether you support more gun control, are an ardent supporter of gun rights or are on the fence, this map of thousands of gun incidents in the U.S. this year sums up a frightening problem .
5. Mixed market opinions The S&P 500 Index SPX, -0.63% declined 7% during October. Ralph Acampora says the market took severe technical damage . Scott Minerd of Guggenheim Partners predicts a bounceback rally followed by a decline of 40% to 50% . But Peter Mallouk expects “ a green wave ,” or sustained rally, following U.S. elections on Nov. 6, no matter which party controls Congress.
6. What you can do to improve your performance if the stock market takes a hard fall October featured the highest volatility for U.S. stocks in 10 years . As usual, most investors with money parked in index funds did nothing. But here are two strategies that may work if you wish to prepare for a bear market:
• Your seven-point guide for the next phase of the stock market
• A simple way to beat a bear market
7. You can’t please everybody Late on Thursday, Apple AAPL, -6.63% reported quarterly earnings and sales that were higher than analysts’ estimates , along with better-than-expected iPhone sales, including average prices. But there was still disappointment . Apple’s shares were down 6% at midday Friday, possibly because the upper end of its holiday sales forecast of $89 billion to $93 billion was only slightly higher than the $92.9 billion estimate among analysts polled by FactSet.
Related: When the going gets tough, Apple hides its numbers
8. Trump fails to focus on good news President Trump should be talking about nothing but the good jobs numbers , but would rather talk about immigration. He also doesn’t take credit for the Bipartisan Budget Act of 2018 .
Something else to think about: Wisconsin taxpayers need to pull the plug on this con of a Foxconn deal
9. How casinos encourage you to lose more money A study at the University of British Columbia details methods used by casino operators and retailers to keep the money flowing .
10. Yes, there is a late-night snack that won’t make you more fat Good news, but you have to keep it whole .
